title: Nucleophilic Addition to the Carbonyl Group
subject: Chemistry
objective: Most reactions of aldehydes and ketones begin with one move. How a nucleophile attacks the polar C=O, and why aldehydes react faster than ketones.

fill.q: During addition, carbon changes from sp² to ____.

tf.q: The nucleophile attacks the carbonyl oxygen.
The alkoxide intermediate is tetrahedral at carbon.
Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones.
Alkyl groups increase the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon.
tf.explain: They release electrons and reduce it.

ar.r: Ketones have two alkyl groups around the carbonyl carbon.

ar.a: The carbonyl carbon is attacked by nucleophiles.
ar.r: Oxygen pulls electrons and leaves carbon delta plus.

mcq.q: The first step of the mechanism is:
mcq.explain: The nucleophile attacks the delta plus carbon.

short.q: Write the steps of nucleophilic addition in order.
short.solution: Nucleophile attacks the carbon, pi electrons move to oxygen, a tetrahedral alkoxide forms, it takes a proton.

short.q: Give two reasons why aldehydes are more reactive than ketones.
short.solution: Steric: less crowding. Electronic: fewer electron-releasing alkyl groups, so carbon is more positive.
